No reply to the US paper, no word on tanker #147. The Houthis deny striking Madinah (AFP). Al Mayadeen was not reached. || OCT 1 19:00 — Tehran denies, through IRNA and Fars, Bloomberg's report that Araghchi offered to let inspectors into the bombed nuclear sites in return for sanctions relief. Quds Force commander Qaani says the US was 'expelled from Iraq' and faces a 'humiliating' position from Lebanon to Iraq; Press TV carries Putin calling the world 'amazed' by Iranian 'courage', and the Foreign Ministry summons the UK envoy over the Fairford accusation. The strait authority's 'non-compliance list' statement stands as the regime's account of this week's tanker strikes. Houthi television reports 'Saudi aggression' on Sanaa and three provinces. Al Mayadeen was not reached. || OCT 1 15:00 — Tehran's strait authority says the three Emirati tankers struck this week were on its non-compliance list and warns owners, charterers and insurers that listed ships face fines, detention or confiscation; Fars reports a supertanker 'travelling illegally' burning off Oman. That is the regime describing the strikes as enforcement. Press TV's front page leads with a 'false-flag hijacking' story about the FlyDubai case and the defence chief's line that American 'war dramas' cannot hide exhaustion; it reports explosions in Sanaa as Saudi strikes. The UN mission thanks Russia and China for the veto. Still no reply to the US paper. Al Mayadeen was not reached. || OCT 1 11:00 — Still no answer to the American paper. Pezeshkian's line hardened through the day: Washington broke the June MOU by keeping the blockade and should drop the idea of 'bringing us to our knees'. An IRGC adviser claims long-range ballistic missiles that hit moving targets, achieved 'in the past few days' — a claim aimed at ships, not shown. The UN mission says nobody expelled the delegation. Press TV leads with the adviser's 'commit suicide' line and says nothing on Madinah or the FlyDubai accusation. Al Mayadeen was not reached. || OCT 1 07:00 — Tehran still has not answered the American paper. Pezeshkian says Iran 'has never avoided' dialogue though it was attacked three times while negotiating. The Guards talk past the talks: the US exit from Iraq is a 'historic victory', 'America must leave the region', Washington will stop 'unless it wants to commit suicide'; spokesman Mohebbi is quoted saying 'we have been hitting small ships … America does not respond' (single source). The rial slid again, to 258,300. || OCT 1 03:00 — Tehran has the American answer and has not replied. Araghchi collected it from the Qataris in Doha on Tuesday and took it to Wednesday's cabinet; the spokeswoman confirms the document and nothing else. Around it the Guards talk past the diplomats: a 'letter to the American people' saying the war ends when the US 'admits defeat' and leaves, the Iraq withdrawal hailed as a 'historic victory', an adviser saying Washington will stop 'unless it wants to commit suicide', Rezaei's 'he can neither negotiate nor fight'. Press TV's frame this morning: 'Trump's Iran gamble turns into a search for an exit'. Al Mayadeen was not reached. The rial is at 257,500. || Two voices, on purpose. The president's: Pezeshkian told the General Assembly on Wednesday that Iran will 'never bow our head, or bend the knee' and is 'ready for dialogue and diplomacy without accepting the language of force', held up the photographs of the assassinated Leader and the Minab schoolgirls, and called the United States 'the victims' maker of terrorists' — the US and Israeli delegations walked out. The soldiers': Safavi, the Leader's military adviser, said any force 'attempting to land in Iran will certainly be destroyed', that Iran's radars follow US warships from the Gulf to the Indian Ocean, and that the strait reopens only when the blockade lifts and Iran's terms are met — Oman, he says, has a mechanism and Washington 'obstructs' it; the Armed Forces promised a reply 'more severe than previous'; Abdollahi: 'no security for aggressors'. Underneath both, the channel is real for the first time since Islamabad: Baghaei confirms 'another round of message exchange and clarification ... through the Qatari mediator' in New York on Tuesday — two hours by his count, three by Trump's, with Witkoff and Kushner across the table — and lists four conditions 'conveyed ... in a manner that leaves no doubt or ambiguity': end the blockade and the 'aggressive actions', end the war on all fronts, release the blocked assets, recognise the Iran–Oman corridor. Rezaei says the same terms went to Qatar and Pakistan; Fars called the Reuters/Kyodo 'reopen in seven days' report 'unreliable and inaccurate'. Nobody in Tehran has claimed the Cape Dao (Sep 23, one Indian seafarer killed) or the LR Stephanie/Al Maryah pair (Sep 21); Al Mayadeen's index, still behind Cloudflare, carries 'IRGC targets 2 ships near Hormuz after repeat US violations' (undated) beside 'Strait of Hormuz closed until Trump, Netanyahu, removed' and 'Iran denies US crossed Hormuz, calls claims fabricated' — the framing is that the strait is Iran's to close and no US convoy has passed. The airline shutdown took effect Wednesday (flights to Turkey, the UAE and China cancelled; Oman, Azerbaijan and Georgia closed their skies); the rial answered at 234,900, weaker by 4,400 in three days. The NPT bill is still paper. ADDENDUM, Thursday 07:00 daily: the soldiers spoke again before Xi sat down — Safavi (Press TV, 09:33 GMT) said new US or Israeli attacks would take the war 'beyond the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz', that Iran keeps control of the strait, and that Chinese vessels may pass; Pezeshkian told Europe to rethink its snapback line; an IRGC official told Al Mayadeen on Tuesday that 'the war is still ongoing, the strait is not open and the US is lying'. At home, the IRGC announced that Brig Gen Hossein Zarifi, head of the Shahid Sajjad base, was killed in an operation at Saravan on Wednesday — no adversary named. Nobody in Tehran has claimed the six missiles at Yanbu and Taif; nobody has confirmed a second round in New York. The rial firmed by 200 to 234,700. ADDENDUM, Thursday 11:00: Tehran put its price in public and its hand in private on the same afternoon. In public, Rezaei (IRIB): seven conditions, the Americans have four to five days, and 'neither the Strait of Hormuz will be opened nor negotiations begin' before they are met; the IRGC's Vahidi and the army's Hatami echoed the president's 'we do not fear war'. In private, by Reuters' count of six sources, a senior Iranian official sketched the phased way out — 'the first [stage] would be to end the blockade and reopen Hormuz' — and regional sources say the transit-fee demand can go into a side attachment because the blockade hurts more than the toll is worth; the same official: 'our fingers are on the trigger'. The Houthis claimed 'dozens' of missiles and drones on Saudi positions at al-Tuwal and al-Daghareer in Jizan (no Saudi confirmation); Moscow's Ulyanov said IAEA inspectors cannot return while Washington threatens daily. The rial firmed to 234,200. Al Mayadeen was not reached (Cloudflare) — no new carry since Tuesday's 'the strait is not open'. ADDENDUM, Thursday 15:00: Tehran claimed its hit and sharpened its threat. The IRGC posted video of the cargo ship burning in the strait — 'at least one projectile struck the violating vessel' — which is the first claim of responsibility for the Cape Dao, the sixty-second UKMTO report and the first death at sea since the El Gaia. By evening the IRGC's Intelligence Unit put every US asset 'on land and water, including US warships' under 'the threat of continuous and sustained strikes' and claimed the Americans are dispersing to Jordan and going underground — intent, not fire. Ghalibaf mocked the ten-year at 5.1% ('the floor two years out … bell-bottoms'); Araghchi asked Europe to 'confront US aggression'; Kata'ib Hezbollah asked Iraqis to break the 'siege'. The rial held at 234,200. ADDENDUM, Thursday 19:00: Tehran put a clock on the table and widened its threat. Araghchi told reporters in New York that Iran handed the mediators a seven-day plan this week — meet the conditions and the strait opens on the seventh day, then talks toward a final deal; Pezeshkian said out loud that Iran wants the Americans 'back in the MoU before the midterms'. The same evening the deputy foreign minister told Europe its bases 'will not go unanswered', and the Indian seamen's union said the Cape Dao took two torpedoes. The rial held at 234,200. ADDENDUM, Thursday 23:00: by dawn in the Gulf Tehran had hardened its public line without touching the channel. Rezaei: until the conditions are met the strait stays shut 'and we will not negotiate'; an Iranian source called the New York contacts 'workshops to explore positions'; Pezeshkian told Fox that America 'must choose', and that the Houthis answer for themselves. The IRGC's intelligence arm claimed the Americans had been forced to disperse and dig in. Reuters, meanwhile, had six sources on a phased sequence — blockade off, strait open, then the rest — and Tehran ready to park its transit fee. The rial held at 234,200. ADDENDUM, Friday 03:00: Tehran's spokesman put the New York contact on the record — Qatar-mediated, Iran's conditions conveyed 'very clearly': fighting ends on all fronts, the blockade and the economic war stop, the assets come back. Ghalibaf told parliament the enemy had been 'taught a valuable lesson'; Mehr counted 313,000 at a national-defence rally; a lawmaker said there would be no Pezeshkian–Trump meeting. The squeeze on Iran's airlines reached Najaf, where Iraq halted every Iranian flight at 23:00 GMT — the first neighbour to act since Rezaei's warning. The rial firmed a shade to 233,900. ADDENDUM, Friday 07:00: Araghchi gave the paper a shape — seven days: guns silent on every front including Lebanon, the blockade and the oil sanctions lifted, the assets released, the strait open at the end of the seventh day, the nuclear file after; 'the moment they accept this plan … this timetable can start'. Rezaei's 'not until the conditions are met' and the president's 'America must choose' framed it; Qatar's prime minister hosted Pezeshkian on de-escalation. Araghchi told Lavrov the US had reneged on the Islamabad understanding and briefed him on the Oman shipping lanes. The airline squeeze reached all four Iraqi airports, and the Leader's adviser answered that regional flights would be 'open to everyone or to no one'. The rial firmed to 233,600. ADDENDUM, Friday 11:00: Tehran worked the Arab side of the table. Araghchi sat with Saudi Arabia's Faisal bin Farhan in New York — IRIB's footage, no Saudi readout yet — after Egypt's Abdelatty took up 'proposals being put forward', and Pakistan's Sharif told the Assembly that Islamabad's mediation goes on. At home the aviation authority stopped selling tickets to Iraq once all four Iraqi airports had shut Iranian carriers out, giving Mokhber's 'everyone or no one' a first, bloodless act. The army's voice was technical: capabilities 'reconfigured', the Arash drone upgraded, cheap missiles to drain the enemy's magazines. Nothing was fired at sea or at the Americans; two US tankers flew over the UAE unmolested. The rial held at 233,600. ADDENDUM, Friday 15:00: Tehran put a clock on the table. Araghchi, to reporters at the UN: the seven days start 'as soon as the United States accepts this plan' — 'if they accept this plan tomorrow, the seven days will start from tomorrow'; the American steps are 'all already in the MoU' and could be done in four or five days; the strait opens on day six, the talks resume on day seven; 'the choice now rests with the United States'. The National's sources say the roadmap carries a term he did not say aloud: dilute the 60% stockpile, then send it out under IAEA mechanisms — and a warning that if nothing comes by the end of the period, military operations could resume. Rezaei kept the other hand up: 'until our conditions are met, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened'. The IRGC's spokesman called Iran the victor and the strait a proof that Washington cannot keep it open 'for even a few hours'.
